claims.claim: The CI diff failure in T-26271 is an unrecognized consequence of the impersonation design in RFC-001: the reporter blames the cluster Secret credential ('the cluster Secret credential itself is broad, so we don't understand why the diff suddenly runs with a narrower identity'), but RFC-001 makes operations run as the AppProject-mapped destination service account once the flag the reporter just enabled is on, so the forbidden 'is attempting to grant RBAC permissions not currently held' error is the narrow per-namespace SA lacking patch on cluster-scoped resources, not a credential regression — the ticket should be read as an impersonation coverage gap, not a cluster-Secret bug.

T-26443's stale-manifest auto-sync is the direct failure mode of RFC-002's push-to-stage design: the RFC states that in push-to-stage mode 'Argo CD relies on some external system to move changes to the deployment branch', and the ticket observes the bug only in that mode because auto-sync deploys whatever the stage branch last held while the external promoter lags — so the ticket is evidence that the RFC's promotion integration point ships without any freshness contract, which changes how the RFC's mode should be evaluated before rollout.

T-28511's delete/recreate infinite loop is field evidence against the PRD's 'No immediate Risks to consider' section: the ticket's ApplicationSet configures the PRD's reverse deletion order, whose defining mechanism ('Waits for one application to be fully deleted before moving onto the next application') is exactly what never completes when a resource is stuck Progressing, causing the controller to restart the wave — so the PRD's Reverse strategy needs a stuck-deletion timeout or escape hatch that its Risks and Mitigations section currently claims is unnecessary.

T-27833's proposed fix (split resources between the control-plane SA and the impersonated SA, removing namespace permissions from the latter) requires reopening a question RFC-001 has already answered and closed: the RFC explicitly resolves that 'The service account to be used for impersonation is determined on a per Application level rather than on per resource level', so the ticket cannot be implemented on the current design and should be read as a change request against RFC-001, not a configuration gap.

The strategy document and the PRD make incompatible commitments about ApplicationSet child deletion: the strategy states 'Deletion of generated Applications is explicitly out of scope for rollout orchestration: ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children will not be implemented' with teardown remaining a manual per-Application operator action, while the PRD's stated goals are precisely to ship automated ordered deletion (deletionOrder AllAtOnce/Reverse) for ApplicationSet children — both cannot hold, and note-2 records the team noticing this without deciding it.

RFC-001 commits that impersonation 'can be enabled/disabled only at the system level. Once enabled/disabled, it is applicable to all Argo CD Applications', but the platform sync call decided the rollout 'goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide' — the org has committed to a rollout granularity the accepted design cannot express, so either the RFC's system-level toggle must be redesigned or the rollout decision cannot be executed as decided.

T-27327's rollback design violates RFC-002's foundational invariant: the RFC requires that 'Every deployed change must have a corresponding dry commit - i.e. git is always the source of any changes' and builds its promotion model on dry-commit lineage, while the ticket proposes rollback that checks out old rendered manifests directly onto the sync branch (explicitly bypassing the staging branch, and explicitly because 'the dry source in git does not fully capture the inputs to rendering') — producing a deployed state with no originating dry commit, which breaks the lineage rules the RFC says promotion systems will depend on.

Rolling out the manifest hydrator systemically amplifies the T-27875 auto-sync deadlock: the hydrator turns every dry change into machine-generated commits on shared sync branches (one hydrated commit per dry commit, per environment branch), sharply raising the probability that a new commit lands while a previous sync is still in progress — which is exactly the condition under which T-27875 leaves apps OutOfSync indefinitely for automated policies without selfHeal — so hydrator adoption converts a rare race into a routine production failure without either document saying so.

The org's two flagship initiatives, the manifest hydrator and progressive sync, are operationally incompatible today: every hydrator cycle lands a fresh commit on the hydrated branch that child Applications treat as a source change (observed on the T-27949 pilot and confirmed at the incident review to restart the rolling sync wave each time), so any repo adopting both features can never complete a rollout wave — a program-level collision that no single design document acknowledges, and which also undermines T-24578's request to bring the hydrator to ApplicationSets.

In push-to-stage mode the correctness of production deploys rests on an external promoter that the org has just admitted is 'still the shell script, nobody owns it': RFC-002 delegates moving hydrated manifests to the deployment branch to that external system, and T-26443 shows the concrete failure when it lags — auto-sync silently deploys whatever stale manifests the branch last held — so an unowned, unmonitored shell script is now a single point of failure for deploy freshness, a risk visible only by combining the RFC's design, the ticket's symptom, and the note's ownership admission.

RFC-002's own suggested integrity controls for the new push-capable component cannot actually be enabled: the RFC introduces a commit server holding repository write credentials and says the security story should recommend enabling features like branch protection, but T-28239 establishes that the hydrator always pushes unsigned commits and that enabling signature verification on the hydrated branch makes Argo CD reject its own output — so until commit signing ships, the sole control protecting the deploy branch from a compromised or spoofed pusher is the write credential itself, a weaker posture than either document individually implies.

proposals.change: Add the root cause established at the platform sync call: with impersonation enabled, the diff runs as the destination service account, which does not hold patch on cluster-scoped resources — the breadth of the cluster Secret credential is not the cause and is not worth chasing further.
proposals.citedLine: the CI diff failures (the missing-permissions one, T-26271) got root-caused on the call: with impersonation on, diff runs as the destination service account which doesn't hold patch on cluster-scoped stuff. someone should note the root cause on that ticket so the reporter stops chasing the cluster secret.

proposals.change: Record that this work is deprioritized to next quarter; the dev pair assigned to it moves to the progressive sync deletion work instead.
proposals.citedLine: hydrator rollback work (the history & rollback ticket, T-27327) is deprioritized to next quarter. dev pair moves to the progressive sync deletion loop instead. ticket should say so.

proposals.change: Record that the delete/recreate loop reproduced in staging with the reverse deletion order, and that the interim mitigation in the incident runbook is to switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before manually deleting any child Application, until the controller fix lands.
proposals.citedLine: the delete/recreate loop (T-28511) reproduced in staging with the reverse deletion order. mitigation for now: incident runbook says switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting any child app by hand. that's the operational rule until the controller fix lands — worth remembering as a standing practice.

proposals.change: Add the restriction from the incident review: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until a debounce exists, because each hydrator push was confirmed to restart the rolling sync wave.
proposals.citedLine: the wave-restart thing on hydrated repos: we confirmed each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave. interim call from the review: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there's a debounce. the pilot ticket (T-27949) should carry that restriction so the next team doesn't trip it.

deltas.body: Sync impersonation rolls out behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide, and no project enables it until the diff story is fixed.
deltas.citedLine: impersonation rollout: we decided it goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide. nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed. that's a real decision, not a maybe.

deltas.body: Standing operational practice until the controller fix lands: before manually deleting any child Application of a progressive-sync ApplicationSet, switch the ApplicationSet's deletion order to AllAtOnce.
deltas.citedLine: the delete/recreate loop (T-28511) reproduced in staging with the reverse deletion order. mitigation for now: incident runbook says switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting any child app by hand. that's the operational rule until the controller fix lands — worth remembering as a standing practice.

deltas.body: Hydrator pilot repositories must not use progressive sync until a debounce exists; each hydrator push is confirmed to restart the rolling sync wave.
deltas.citedLine: the wave-restart thing on hydrated repos: we confirmed each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave. interim call from the review: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there's a debounce. the pilot ticket (T-27949) should carry that restriction so the next team doesn't trip it.
